title: Gramigna alla Salsiccia
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Short, curly pasta tubes tossed in a rich, creamy sausage and tomato sauce, a beloved everyday classic from Bologna's home kitchens and neighborhood trattorie alike.
longDesc: Gramigna, named for its resemblance to a weedy grass, is a shape built specifically to catch onto a chunky, meaty sauce, and its pairing with sausage in a light cream-tomato sauce has made it one of Emilia-Romagna's most reliably comforting weeknight dishes.
ingredients: 400 g (14 oz) gramigna pasta (or substitute cavatappi or fusilli)
400 g (14 oz) Italian sausage, casings removed and crumbled
60 ml (1/4 cup) extra virgin olive oil
steps: Warm the olive oil in a large pan and saute the onion until softened.
Add the crumbled sausage and cook until browned, breaking it into small pieces.
Add the wine and let it reduce.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente.
Stir the cream into the sausage sauce and simmer for a few more minutes until slightly thickened.
Drain the pasta, reserving some cooking water, and toss into the sauce with a splash of the water.
Season to taste and serve with grated Parmigiano.
chefTips: Break the sausage into small, even crumbles for the best texture throughout the sauce.
A short simmer after adding the cream helps the sauce properly thicken and cling to the pasta.
Gramigna curly shape is specifically designed to catch onto chunky sauces - a similar tubular, curled pasta works well as a substitute.
commonMistakes: Overcooking the cream sauce, which can cause it to separate rather than stay smooth.
Using bland sausage, which is the primary flavor driver of this simple dish.
Substituting a very smooth, long pasta shape, which won't hold the chunky sauce as well.
servedWith: A medium-bodied red wine from Emilia
storage: The sauce keeps refrigerated for up to 3 days.
reheating: Reheat the sauce gently on the stovetop; cook fresh pasta just before serving.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein from the sausage.
culturalNote: Gramigna alla salsiccia is a beloved everyday classic in Bologna and throughout Emilia-Romagna, a reliable comfort dish found in countless neighborhood trattorie.
